name: Margarites
seoTitle: Margarites, Crete: The Pottery Village Near Rethymno
seoDescription: Margarites is the pottery village of Crete, 30 minutes from Rethymno, where working ceramic workshops still throw and fire by hand. Free to visit and walk.
summary: Margarites is a hillside village about 30 minutes south-east of Rethymno that has made pottery for centuries and still does. The draw is not a museum but working workshops: a dozen or so of them along the main street, where potters throw on the wheel in the open and fire kilns on site, and where what you buy comes from the person who made it. The village itself is stone houses, narrow lanes, Byzantine churches and views across the Mylopotamos valley, and it takes about an hour to walk. It is free to visit and pairs naturally with Arkadi Monastery, ancient Eleftherna and the Melidoni Cave, all within the same short circuit.
body:
## The pottery

Margarites has clay in the ground around it and has been working it since at least the Venetian period. The local tradition is the pithos, the huge storage jar used for oil, wine and grain, and the biggest ones were built up in stages rather than thrown, then fired in wood kilns for days. That trade collapsed when plastic and steel arrived, and the village survives now on smaller domestic ware, glazed and unglazed, sold to visitors.

What makes it worth the drive is that the workshops are genuinely workshops. Wheels are running, kilns are being loaded, and unfinished pieces are drying on shelves outside. Potters are used to people watching and will usually explain what they are doing.

## The village

The main street runs along a shelf on the hillside with the valley dropping away on one side, so almost every cafe terrace has a view. There are Byzantine churches, including Agios Ioannis with fourteenth-century frescoes, and the usual Cretan village fabric of stone houses, external staircases and vines over the lanes. A single square with a couple of tavernas serves as the centre.

## Buying

Prices are workshop prices, and pieces vary in quality because they vary in maker. Ask whether something is food-safe and whether the glaze is lead-free if you intend to use it rather than display it, and expect the potter to give you a straight answer.

## Practicalities

The village is free to enter and about 25 km from Rethymno, half an hour by car. Park at the entrance and walk in; the main street is narrow. An hour is enough unless you stop to eat. Most workshops close for a long afternoon break, so mornings are the reliable time to see anyone working.

faqs.a: Pottery. The village has worked the local clay for centuries and still has around a dozen working ceramic workshops, where you can watch potters at the wheel and buy directly from them.

faqs.q: How far is Margarites from Rethymno?
faqs.a: About 25 km east, roughly 30 minutes by car through the Mylopotamos hills.

faqs.q: Can you watch the potters working?
faqs.a: Yes, in most workshops, and they are used to it. Mornings are more reliable than afternoons, when many close for a break.
No. Margarites is a village, free to walk into and around. You pay only for what you buy or eat.
Arkadi Monastery, the archaeological site and museum of ancient Eleftherna, and the Melidoni Cave are all within a short drive, and the four are usually visited as one day.
